content.comment_body: I am experiencing the same problem, and I have confirmed that I am using the latest [product_name] [version_no]. My [product_name] device has article number [article_no].

A screenshot alone isn't sufficient explanation. We need additional details. What is the IP address and subnet mask of the [product_name] device? What are the IP address and subnet mask of your PC or laptop?
Here is an image showing both the [product_name] device's IP and subnet along with the PC's IP and subnet in the same window.

The [product_name] device and your PC are on different IP subnets, and their subnet masks do not match. An IP address comprises four segments, and with a subnet mask of 255.255.255.0, the first three segments should be identical. Are you using a USB Ethernet adapter?
No, I am connecting it directly to my PC's Ethernet port. How do I resolve this?

You need to set the first three segments of the IP addresses to be the same on both devices. You can either change the IP address of the [product_name] device to match your PC or update your PC's network card IP address to match the [product_name] device.
This fixed the problem. Thank you. [url]

analysis.insight_summary: A user encountered a connection error when trying to access a [product_name] device using [product_name] [version_no]. The issue was traced to mismatched network configuration between the PC and the device, specifically different IP subnets and subnet masks. The discussion highlights the value of accurate network setup and providing detailed diagnostic information to assist troubleshooting.
